issues.description: The problem statement specifies Genre should have a String property named `name` and an optional `subgenre`. In the provided solution the Genre struct declares the property as `genreName` (and thus the synthesized memberwise initializer expects `genreName:`), while the client code and bookstore assembly call `Genre(name: ...)` and access `genre.name`. This name mismatch between the Genre property and the initializer/usage will cause compile errors and contradicts the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Genre struct match the problem specification and client usage: rename the property `genreName` to `name` (i.e. `let name: String`) so the synthesized initializer is `Genre(name:subgenre:)` and client code can access `genre.name`. Alternatively, if you prefer `genreName`, update all client usages and assembly calls to use `genreName:` and access `genre.genreName` consistently.

issues.description: The Problem Statement specifies that Genre has a property name (a String) and an optional subgenre. In the Solution implementation the Genre struct declares the primary property as genreName rather than name, while other parts of the solution (Client) construct Genre using Genre(name: ...) and access genre.name. This mismatch between 'name' and 'genreName' creates a direct identifier naming inconsistency that will confuse students and can cause compilation/runtime mapping errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier across artifacts. Prefer matching the Problem Statement: rename the Genre struct property genreName to name (let name: String) in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift and update any usages accordingly (initializers and accesses). Alternatively, if keeping genreName, update the problem statement and all code usages to use genreName consistently. The first option (rename to name) is recommended to match the exercise text.
